summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, ICD placement, diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for acute on chronic shortness of breath and chest pressure. The symptoms were likely triggered by noncompliance with his daily Lasix regimen. He was treated with intravenous and oral diuretics, and his lisinopril was safely restarted given stable renal function. A stress test showed no evidence of ischemia but revealed a decline in ejection fraction from 36% to 27%, indicating worsening systolic function. His symptoms improved with treatment, and he was discharged home with home health services. He was counseled on medication adherence, sodium restriction, and smoking cessation, with follow-up arranged with cardiology.
